training_data: ADNI AD-dementia/NC 18F-FDG-PET development set (n=487), with a stratified ADNI internal test set (n=73)
test_data: J-ADNI AD-dementia/NC (n=196, Japan) for diagnosis. For prognosis: J-ADNI MCI (n=129) and HABS NC (n=274, Harvard Aging Brain Study), plus ADNI MCI (n=663) internally
reason: The DL classifier was trained on ADNI only, then frozen (the trained model is released on GitHub). It was tested on J-ADNI AD/NC (AUC 0.98, accuracy 90.8% at the fixed 0.5 threshold), and its fixed output was carried into J-ADNI MCI and HABS NC to test prognostic value. The study's own model therefore reaches V4 on cohorts from another consortium and country. Caveat: the prognostic Cox models (clinical + SUVR + DL output) and the DL tertile cut-offs were refitted inside each cohort, so the J-ADNI and HABS iAUCs are not fixed-model external estimates; only the DL score itself is fixed.

quotes.quote: The DL model was developed using the ADNI AD-dementia/NC development set and tested on the ADNI AD-dementia/NC test set, and externally tested on the J-ADNI AD-dementia/NC set to assess the diagnostic performance on an Asian population.

Second, after the DL model development, the prognostic value of DL output for cognitive decline was evaluated in conjunction with clinical features and 18F-FDG-PET SUVR in the ADNI MCI, J-ADNI MCI, and HABS NC sets.

18F-FDG-PET-based DL could distinguish between AD-dementia and NC with AUCs of 0.97 and 0.98, and accuracies of 91.8% and 90.8% on the ADNI AD-dementia/NC test set and the J-ADNI AD-dementia/NC set, respectively.
